prior_importants.description: `competingBranches` ignores the `retired` event that `pup retire` (decision 141) now writes. A retired session keeps its decision numbers on every later gate. Once its gated commit is pruned, it refuses every gate that adds an ADR, with a "PR not landed" line and a fetch remedy.

A PR closed on GitHub without merging is counted as an open PR forever. Its numbers stay taken permanently. If its gated sha is ever pruned, every ADR-adding gate in the repo fails, and nothing in the store can retire the PR.

findings.description: A branch can add `docſ/adr/NNNN-x.md` (long s, U+017F), which git's ASCII-only `icase` pathspec does not match. The ADR stage never sees it, even though APFS folds `ſ` onto `s` and puts the file in `docs/adr/`.
findings.body:
**The case-blind pathspec misses `docſ/adr/`, which APFS treats as `docs/adr/`.**

Both decision listings filter on one pathspec:

```ts
const ADR_PATHSPEC = ':(top,literal,icase)docs/adr/';
```

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/973a8990c05b88c2312fbb2ba362065bb903f4f3/src/core/adr-number.service.ts#L15-L21>

It is used in `addedAdrPaths` (L87) and `decisionRenames` (L125). Git's `icase` folds one byte at a time and only for ASCII, so the UTF-8 bytes `C5 BF` of `ſ` never match `s`. APFS, the gate's filesystem, does fold `ſ` onto `s`. The repo has already measured this: ADR 0110 L89-92 says "`docſ/impl.py -> impl.md` landed on `docs/impl.md` unseen", and `merge-gate.service.ts` notes it in the comment above `NON_ASCII`:

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/973a8990c05b88c2312fbb2ba362065bb903f4f3/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L352-L361>

**Trigger.**
1. A session uses plumbing (`update-index --cacheinfo`) to commit `docſ/adr/0012-x.md`, where 0012 is already on the target.
2. The task's scope-in is broad enough to match the path, e.g. `**`. Scope-in globs match bytes exactly, so `docs/**` would reject it.
3. `addedAdrPaths` returns nothing, so neither `added` nor `misnamed` is set, and `adrNumberStage` returns `undefined` (L326). The gate goes on.

**Wrong result.** On the operator's APFS checkout the file lands in `docs/adr/` next to the target's 0012. Every later gate's `ls-tree --full-tree … docs/adr/` (L270-274) reads only the exact path and never counts it. ADR 0146's *Names* section gives exactly this harm (a name "invisible to every later gate" in the one folder a case-insensitive host gives it) as the reason for the `icase` refusal. Its *Ceilings* section does not accept it.

Nothing else in the gate catches it:
- `NON_ASCII` only feeds the diff-size split and the untested-skip check.
- `core.protectHFS` only guards spellings of `.git`.

Of the letters in `docs/adr`, only `s` has a single non-ASCII character that folds onto it, so one extra pathspec closes the gap.

**Fix direction.** Add the long-s spelling and pass both pathspecs in `addedAdrPaths` and `decisionRenames`:

```ts
const ADR_PATHSPECS = [':(top,literal,icase)docs/adr/', ':(top,literal,icase)docſ/adr/'];
// …
'--', ...ADR_PATHSPECS
```

The path then fails `ADR_DECISION` and is refused as misnamed. `meantAs` already suggests `docs/adr/…`, because `docſ/adr/` has the same UTF-16 length as `ADR_DIR`.

This was validated statically. Git's and APFS's folding behaviour comes from pinned-version knowledge, which is why confidence is medium.

findings.description: `decisionRenames` passes `--find-renames` but no `-l0`. If a session sets `diff.renameLimit=1` in the shared config, a peer's real slug rename (edited text plus another added decision) is refused as "changed too much". This only causes false refusals, not evasion. `merge-gate.service.ts` L229-263 already pins `-l0` against this limit; the fix is to add `'-l0'` after `'--find-renames'`.

process_issues.description:
Round 5 budget: only correctness, security and guards ran.
- conventions, docs, context, simplicity and maintainability were skipped under the round budget.
- workflow-safety was skipped because nothing under .github/workflows changed.
- spec was skipped because there is no closing issue or --spec.

Correctness and security each ran two instances, since the diff is past the size gate (1335 lines). Correctness was split into adr-number.service.ts logic and gate/CLI/dashboard integration. Security was split into git argv/evasion and output/resource bounds.

The review-consolidator was not spawned: only two findings came back, on different root causes, so nothing could be grouped.

The validator confirmed the long-s pathspec finding but suggested a nit, since the trigger needs an adversarial session using plumbing and a broad scope-in. It is kept as important because ADR 0110 precedent fixes every ſ evasion and ADR 0146's Names section targets this harm.

The guards reviewer checked the guard tests only, not prose invariants in the ADRs.

The head was unchanged at 973a899 when re-checked.
